result.summary:
Independently re-read the current lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md Sec 0 (Rework-1 evidence bullet), Sec 6, Sec 7, INV-RB-10, and OQ-5 in full, then independently re-derived (not copied from CODE-DESIGNER's rework summary) the 'no version-scoped correlation exists' claim by reading lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_plan.ex (full file) and lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex (full file) directly, plus lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex's mark_review_applied/2 (lines 284-290) and promotion_review.ex's schema (full file). All six verification points hold:

1. CARDINALITY BRANCHING (Sec 6, INV-RB-10): genuinely specified, not hand-waved. The rewritten lookup is a plain `case matching_reviews do [] -> ...; [single_review] -> ...; [_, _ | _] -> ... end`. Confirmed the `[_, _ | _]` (ambiguous) branch contains no Repo call and no call into Sec 7's supersede_review/3 at all -- it is a single local-variable assignment (superseded_review_id = nil), textually identical in shape to the `[]` branch's own assignment. Sec 7's call site text is explicit that '§6's `[]` and `[_, _ | _]` branches never reach this call at all.' This fully eliminates the original corruption mechanism (blanket-superseding R1/R2/R3 on a multi-promotion history) -- the multi-match case now mutates zero rows, verified structurally, not merely asserted.

2. RETURN-SHAPE AMBIGUITY (superseded_review_id: nil covering both zero-match and refused-ambiguous-match): real but non-blocking. The design's own rollback_result() type comment (Sec 2) states this plainly in-line: 'nil covers BOTH "zero matching reviews" and "more than one matched, ambiguous, none touched" -- see §6' -- this is disclosed, not hidden. Checked whether this distinction matters against REQ-038's actual acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml lines 1814-1819): AC4's literal text is about what happens to DB rows and the event count ('appends exactly one ... event and updates any applied/approved ... row ... to superseded'), not about what information the return value must convey about *why* no row was updated. REQ-038's own description text (line 1810-1811) already establishes 'zero matching rows is acceptable, not an error' as a legitimate non-error outcome with no accompanying reason-code:  the design's extension of that same non-distinguishing nil to the ambiguous case is consistent with an interpretation the requirement itself already commits to, not a new invented ambiguity. Also relevant: no orchestrator caller of rollback_definition_version/4 exists yet (Sec 1's own scope table: HTTP layer is S4, not built here), so there is currently no real caller who would need to act differently on 'zero' vs 'ambiguous' at all. This is a genuine, disclosed design-quality limitation (an observability gap, not a correctness/corruption defect) -- flagged below as non-blocking but worth REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's attention, per this task's own instruction to note it either way.

3. NO VERSION-SCOPED CORRELATION -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED: read promotion_plan.ex's full compute_promotion_plan/5 and its PromotionPlan.t() shape directly. Confirmed target_definition_id/base_version (lines 58-62, populated 160-162) come from fetch_active/2 called at plan-compute time -- they identify the target tenant's row that is active BEFORE the promotion runs (the row later deprecated), never the row the promotion activates. Read promotion.ex's full write_target_definition/5 (lines 220-255) directly: confirmed new_row is a fresh Repo.insert inside Repo.transaction/1 (line 238-254), its id is a newly minted UUID that does not exist at plan-compute time. Read append_promotion_event/9 (lines 289-323) directly: confirmed event_attrs (lines 300-309) computes target_definition_id: new_row.id together with review_id: review.id in one map -- this actually is the one place the correlation is computed -- but it is handed only to the injected event_appender closure (line 311), never persisted to any table this function touches. Read promotion_review_store.ex's mark_review_applied/2 (lines 284-290) directly: confirmed it calls transition/6 with set_fn returning only `[status: :applied]` -- no definition_id-shaped field exists on PromotionReview's schema (confirmed against promotion_review.ex's full `schema "promotion_reviews" do` block, lines 71-90: tenant_id, plan_digest, def_type, def_id (:string), serialised_plan, status, requested_by, approved_by, approved_at, superseded_by, row_version -- no definition_id field) to write it to even if mark_review_applied/2 wanted to. This independently reconfirms the design's own Sec 0 Rework-1 evidence bullet claim exactly, line-range citations included, and rules out any overlooked persisted correlation.

4. OQ-5 HONEST DISCLOSURE: confirmed OQ-5 (Sec 10) is rewritten from 'RESOLVED in Rework 1' framing that states plainly 'AC4 is satisfied exactly for the unambiguous case and is honestly *not* fully realized for a process_key with more than one accumulated applied/approved review -- a real, disclosed limitation of the current schema, not a gap this design papers over,' and explicitly asks REVIEWER to 'confirm this tradeoff (safety over completeness, within REQ-038's declared scope) is acceptable, or route the follow-up to REQ-ANALYST if not.' This does not silently claim full AC4 compliance. Judged against docs/requirements.yaml's actual AC4 wording (grepped and read directly, lines 1814-1819: 'a successful rollback appends exactly one DEFINITION_VERSION_ROLLED_BACK event and updates any applied/approved promotion_reviews row for the former-active definition to superseded'): the requirement's own description text already treats zero-match as a legitimate non-error outcome, and the ambiguous-match scenario is structurally impossible to have existed in R-Co's own schema (where def_id genuinely was a definition-scoped UUID) -- REQ-038's authors could not have anticipated this Letflow-specific schema translation consequence. Treating 'ambiguous' the same as the already-accepted 'zero-match' outcome, while flagging it explicitly for REVIEWER sign-off rather than silently deciding it, is a reasonable and adequately-disclosed reading, not an unrequested unilateral reinterpretation -- it follows exactly the escalation pattern core-directives.md requires ('don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled' -- this design does not decide it, it surfaces the tradeoff for REVIEWER). Concrete, buildable Path 3 (a promotion_reviews.definition_id column + a new mark_review_applied/3 arity) is fully specified in Sec 6's 'Recommended follow-up' subsection for REQ-ANALYST/REVIEWER to pick up later, not left as a vague TBD.

5. DIFF SCOPE CHECK: ran `git diff 3cda9b5 6b86058 -- lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md` directly. Confirmed the diff touches only: the Rework-1 provenance note (top of doc), a new Sec 0 evidence bullet, Sec 1's scope-table wording (non-substantive), Sec 2's return-type comment, Sec 5 Step 4's prose, Sec 6 (rewritten), Sec 7's call-site scoping sentence, INV-RB-10 (new), OQ-5 (rewritten), and Sec 11's AC4 traceability row. Sec 3 (status-enum mapping), OQ-3 (transaction-boundary), Sec 7's core :approved-widening rationale/edit spec, Sec 4.1/Sec 5 Step 1 (permission-guard ordering), and the index-predicate MINOR finding do not appear anywhere in the diff -- confirmed untouched, not merely claimed untouched.

6. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: `git show --stat 6b86058` confirms the rework commit touched only lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md and its own handoff JSON -- no .ex/.exs file anywhere in the diff. The new Sec 6 case-block uses the same pseudocode density/style as the already-passed Sec 5 algorithm blocks (Repo.update_all/Enum.find literals) -- consistent with this document's established, previously-accepted style, not a new implementation-code violation introduced by this rework.

Verdict: the rework genuinely resolves the corruption risk (BLOCKER from the prior FAIL) with concrete, structurally-verified logic and honest, explicit disclosure of the resulting partial-AC4-satisfaction limitation. PASS.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md Sec 2's rollback_result().superseded_review_id is nil for both the zero-match case (nothing needed superseding) and the ambiguous multi-match case (something needed superseding but the design refuses to guess). The design discloses this plainly in the type comment and in Sec 6/OQ-5, so it is not a hidden gap, and it does not cause any data corruption -- but a future caller (once an S4 HTTP layer or an orchestrator exists) has no way to distinguish these two outcomes from the return value alone, which could matter for audit/operator visibility into 'a rollback landed in an ambiguous-review state that needs manual review.' Not a blocker: AC4's literal wording does not require the return value to convey a reason code, REQ-038's own description text already treats zero-match as a legitimate non-distinguished non-error outcome, and no current caller exists to be affected. Recommend REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR explicitly confirm this tradeoff is acceptable (or that a future requirement should add a distinct :ambiguous_reviews_skipped-shaped signal) rather than this passing through unexamined.

OQ-5's accepted resolution means AC4 as literally written ('updates any applied/approved promotion_reviews row for the former-active definition to superseded') is only fully satisfied when exactly one applied/approved promotion_reviews row exists for the process_key at rollback time; for a process_key with more than one accumulated applied/approved review (an ordinary state for any process_key promoted more than once, per the design's own Sec 6 analysis), the promotion_reviews-update portion of AC4 does not fire even though the event-append portion still does. This is honestly disclosed by the design (not silently papered over) and is forced by a genuine Letflow schema limitation (def_id is process-key-scoped, not version-scoped) that did not exist in R-Co's own schema this requirement was ported from. Flagging per this task's explicit instruction: RELEASE-VALIDATOR should specifically re-scrutinize, at Step 5, whether this partial-satisfaction interpretation of AC4 is acceptable before REQ-038 is marked done, rather than treating CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's PASS here as having settled that judgment call.

result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a) and/or FRONTEND-DEV (Step 2b, not applicable -- backend-only) to implement lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md. Carry both MINOR issues above forward into RELEASE-VALIDATOR's Step 5 scrutiny list for REQ-038 -- neither blocks Step 2a, both concern whether AC4's partial-satisfaction interpretation should ultimately be accepted as 'done' or routed to REQ-ANALYST for a follow-up schema requirement.
